name: Intimate washes/cleansers
native_basis: mucosal-contact cosmetic — finished product as sold, total content basis (rinse-off surfactant cleanser applied to vulvar mucosa; vulvovaginal mucosal application). Read across the strictest sovereign mucosal-contact cosmetic contaminant tier, not the general dermal-cosmetic tier. Not a leachate/migration number.
exposure_pathway: Vulvovaginal mucosal (more permeable and bioavailable than intact skin) and, for internal devices, prolonged internal contact

Pb.label: German BVL 2017 sovereign mucosal-contact cosmetic tier (toothpaste, 500 ug/kg)
Pb.mucosal_note: Adopted over the general-cosmetic lead tier (2000 ug/kg) because vaginal mucosa is more permeable and bioavailable than the oral mucosa the toothpaste limit was written for; 500 ug/kg is the strictest sovereign cosmetic lead value for a mucosal-contact product.

Cd.basis_note: Cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury bind the strictest general-cosmetic sovereign value (German BVL 2017 = the strictest cosmetic tier for these three); no stricter mucosal-contact tier exists for them, so no further mucosal adjustment applies. Lead binds the stricter sovereign mucosal-contact tier (500 vs the general-cosmetic 2000 ug/kg), because vaginal mucosa is more permeable than the oral mucosa the toothpaste tier was written for.

tAs.binding_scope: cosmetic products in general except theater, fan, or carnival make-up
tAs.basis_note: Cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury bind the strictest general-cosmetic sovereign value (German BVL 2017 = the strictest cosmetic tier for these three); no stricter mucosal-contact tier exists for them, so no further mucosal adjustment applies. Lead binds the stricter sovereign mucosal-contact tier (500 vs the general-cosmetic 2000 ug/kg), because vaginal mucosa is more permeable than the oral mucosa the toothpaste tier was written for.

iAs.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic; no jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for any feminine-care product. It is governed by reflex speciation: whenever total arsenic is elevated, inorganic arsenic is speciated by HPLC-ICP-MS, and the inorganic fraction is held under ALARA and bounded by the total-arsenic ceiling (bounded by the total-arsenic cosmetic ceiling).
iAs.reference_method: Reflex HPLC-ICP-MS inorganic-arsenic speciation triggered by an elevated total-arsenic screen.

tHg.basis_note: Cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury bind the strictest general-cosmetic sovereign value (German BVL 2017 = the strictest cosmetic tier for these three); no stricter mucosal-contact tier exists for them, so no further mucosal adjustment applies. Lead binds the stricter sovereign mucosal-contact tier (500 vs the general-cosmetic 2000 ug/kg), because vaginal mucosa is more permeable than the oral mucosa the toothpaste tier was written for.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury forms by microbial methylation in aquatic food webs and bioaccumulates in fish muscle; an aqueous or leave-on intimate cosmetic has no methylation pathway and no dietary mercury source. Intimate-product metal surveys measure TOTAL mercury, not methylmercury, so no routed source reports methylmercury (the not-material integrity gate is speciation-aware). Any mercury present is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury control/ceiling. No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for a menstrual or intimate-care product.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No MeHg ML for any menstrual/intimate-care product in any jurisdiction; methylmercury MLs are scoped to fish and seafood only.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: 21 CFR 884 & EU MDR 2017/745 (device biocompatibility, no content ML); Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, China NMPA 2015, ASEAN 2019, Korea MFDS 2024/2025, FDA 21 CFR 700 (cosmetic contaminant limits — none set MeHg)

Ni.binding_scope: cosmetic products other than eye makeup or color makeup products
Ni.basis_note: Nickel binds the only sovereign cosmetic nickel content limit (Korea MFDS 2025, cosmetic products other than eye/color makeup, 10000 ug/kg). Under the mucosal route the program additionally holds nickel to ALARA post-publication (a known contact sensitizer).

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium content limit for cosmetics; chromium can enter an intimate cosmetic as a trace contaminant of colorants and mineral raw materials. Held under a reflex screen (test every lot; ALARA), not declared not-material.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on each lot; reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any elevated total-chromium result.

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is never a panel number; it is the toxic species obtained by reflex speciation. No jurisdiction sets a Cr(VI) content limit for any feminine-care product. Any lot whose total-chromium screen is elevated is speciated for Cr(VI); any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Reflex IC-ICP-MS Cr(VI) speciation (EPA 3060A alkaline extraction + EPA 6800 / EN 15192) on an elevated total-chromium screen.

Sn.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a tin content limit for any cosmetic, and an aqueous surfactant or leave-on intimate cosmetic has no tin source: tin migrates into a product only from tinplate/can contact, which is absent for a bottled, tubed, or sachet cosmetic. No routed source reports tin in a feminine-cosmetic product. Rebuttable and audited against the register and routed corpus each build.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No cosmetic tin ML in any jurisdiction; no tinplate-contact pathway for a bottled/sachet intimate cosmetic.
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: Germany BVL 2017; Health Canada; China NMPA 2015; ASEAN 2019; Korea MFDS 2024/2025; FDA 21 CFR 700

Al.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium content limit for cosmetics; aluminium is a ubiquitous trace constituent of cosmetic raw materials and may be present at higher levels in feminine deodorants. This control governs CONTAMINANT aluminium under a reflex screen (ALARA on the mucosal route); a product formulated with an intentional aluminium active is out of scope for the aluminium contaminant cell and evaluated separately.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on each lot; held under ALARA against the tightest available context.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Device forms carry no sovereign heavy-metal content limit, so every panel cell resolves to a mandatory analytical control or a substantiated not-material determination; no occurrence percentile is computed and no number is invented. Cosmetic forms read across the strictest sovereign mucosal-contact cosmetic contaminant limit. Two basis families (device content, cosmetic content) are never conflated, and neither is a leachate/migration number. Provenance vocabulary: {regulatory-alignment, read-across, not-material, control, ratchet}.
lineage_note: Initial Cat-15 Feminine Care government-limit standard (HMTc Method v2.0). Flagship mucosal-exposure category. Device subcategories (tampons, pads, cups, discs, period underwear, other) carry no sovereign heavy-metal content limit (medical-device law governs ISO 10993 biocompatibility, not content) and resolve to mandatory control on every occurrence- or pathway-established metal (Pb, Cd, tAs, tHg, Ni, Cr, Sn, Al; iAs and Cr-VI reflex-speciation controls); methylmercury is the sole not-material cell (no biological methylation pathway; bounded by the total-mercury control). Cosmetic subcategories (feminine wipes, deodorants, douches, intimate washes) read across the German BVL 2017 sovereign cosmetic contaminant limits, adopting the mucosal-contact (toothpaste) tier for lead (500 vs the general-cosmetic 2000 ug/kg) because vaginal mucosa is more permeable than the oral mucosa those limits were written for; Cd/tAs/tHg bind the strictest general-cosmetic value (100/500/100), nickel the only sovereign cosmetic Ni limit (Korea MFDS 2025 = 10000). Materiality anchored to shearston2024, ica2024, ellison2026, carlin2020, nic-corcrain2025, marcelis2024. Direction: toward the literature (CLAUDE.md Part 2/19).
